---
title: "Configuring a project"
subtitle: "One YAML file describes a basin, and every workflow reads it"
---

The toolbox has no command-line interface and no per-workflow settings files.
Everything a run needs comes from **one configuration file**, passed to every
workflow as `--configfile`.

Start from `config/templates/snake_config.template.yml`, which annotates every
option inline. `test_case/snake_config_baseline.yml` is a filled-in worked
example, and `test_case/snake_config_rapid.yml` is the same basin sized for a
quick end-to-end run.

::: {.callout-important}
## Two path rules that catch people out

**Paths inside a config resolve against the directory you run Snakemake from**
(the repository root), not against the config file's own location. So
`project_dir: test_case/test_rapid` means the same thing wherever the config
lives.

**For real work, point `project_dir` outside the repository tree.** Run outputs
are not source. The in-repo `test_case/` projects are a development convention
only.
:::

Keep the config **next to the project it writes into**, the way the shipped
examples sit beside theirs. That is how a real project is laid out.

## Anatomy

Three blocks, in this order.

### `project:` — where things live

```yaml
project:
  project_dir: test_case/test_rapid
  static_dir: config
  data_sources: config/catalogs/deltares_data.yml
  data_sources_climate: config/catalogs/cmip6_data.yml
```

`data_sources` and `data_sources_climate` name **HydroMT data catalogs**. Every
dataset a run reads is registered in a catalog and referenced by name — data
paths are never written directly into a workflow.

### `shared:` — the basin, and the period, that all workflows agree on

```yaml
shared:
  basin:
    region: "{'subbasin': [9.666, 0.4476], 'uparea': 100}"
    resolution: 0.00833
    gauge_points: test_case/test_data/output_locations.csv
  historical_window:
    starttime: "2000-01-01T00:00:00"
    endtime: "2016-12-31T00:00:00"
  clim_historical: era5
```

- **`region`** is a HydroMT region specification. The example delineates the
  subbasin draining to a point at (9.666 °E, 0.4476 °N) with at least 100 km² of
  upstream area.
- **`historical_window`** sizes the historical climate store. The weather
  generator needs a floor of historical years to work from; a window shorter than
  the toolbox-wide minimum is refused at parse time rather than producing a
  quietly degraded stress test.
- **`clim_historical`** is the forcing dataset the model is driven with. Because
  the toolbox does no local calibration, this is the single most consequential
  setting in the file — which is what workflow 0 exists to inform.

### `workflows:` — one subsection per workflow

Each carries an `enabled:` flag plus its own settings:

```yaml
workflows:
  analyze_climate:
    enabled: true
    candidate_sources: [chirps]     # makes wf0 a comparison, not a single-source figure set
  build_model:
    enabled: true
    model_build_config: config/defaults/wflow_build_model.yml
    wflow_outvars: ['river discharge', 'actual evapotranspiration', 'groundwater recharge']
    simulation_window:
      starttime: "2010-01-01T00:00:00"
      endtime: "2016-12-31T00:00:00"
  analyze_projections:
    enabled: true
    clim_project: cmip6
    models: [NOAA-GFDL/GFDL-ESM4, INM/INM-CM4-8]
    scenarios: [ssp245]
  run_stress_test:
    enabled: true
```

`enabled:` must be a real boolean — unquoted `true`/`false`/`yes`/`no`/`on`/`off`.
A quoted `"true"` or an integer `1` is rejected rather than guessed at. A missing
`enabled:` key is a hard error naming the absent key, not a silent default.

::: {.callout-warning}
## `enabled: false` skips the run, it does not clean up after it

Disabling a workflow means the wrapper does not invoke it. Its previous outputs
are neither deleted nor refreshed, so an enabled downstream workflow consumes
whatever is already on disk. Staleness is yours to reason about.
:::

## Where the other configuration lives

| Directory | What it is | Do you edit it? |
|---|---|---|
| `config/catalogs/` | HydroMT data catalogs — the `-d` targets | Yes, to register a data source |
| `config/defaults/` | Build configs a rule actually reads (`wflow_build_model.yml`, `wflow_update_waterbodies.yml`, `weathergen_config.yml`) | Yes — changing one changes a run |
| `config/templates/` | Scaffolds you copy, including the config template above | Copy, don't edit in place |
| `config/advanced_settings.yml` | Toolbox-wide limits and defaults, read for every project | Rarely |

`config/advanced_settings.yml` is **not** a `--configfile` target — it is read
once, for every project. It holds hard constraints no project config can relax
(such as the minimum number of historical years), defaults a project config may
override, and external toolchain pins. Its schema is closed: an unknown key is
rejected at parse time rather than ignored.

::: {.callout-note}
## On Linux

Use the `*_linux.yml` variants of both the config and the data catalog — the
data-catalog paths differ from Windows.
:::

## Naming an experiment

`workflows.run_stress_test.experiment_name` is optional. Left unset, the stress
test names the experiment after the project plus the date it was first created,
and **reuses** an existing dated experiment rather than minting today's date — so
incremental re-runs keep landing in the same place.

To pin a deliberate name (a scenario label, or a second experiment beside the
first), run this **once, before the first stress-test run**:

```bash
pixi run python scripts/suggest_experiment_name.py <your config> --name dry_scenario
```

It reserves the directory atomically and writes the key back into your config,
leaving comments and layout intact. An existing value is never overwritten: the
experiment directory is what a completed run's outputs are addressed by, so
renaming it would strand them. Clear the key by hand to go back to the default.
